latin: Qui dixerit personas in diuinis absolutis proprietatibus distingui, catholicae ueritati non repugnabit.
translation: Whoever says that the Persons are distinguished in God by absolute properties will not be at odds with Catholic truth.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch5, from Latin at farmer1998:12149
attribution: Reports Duns Scotus, third of the theses drawn from his work, part of a series beginning at 2.1 (farmer1998:12135, 12214).

sources.text: John Duns Scotus, Ordinatio 1, distinction 8, part 1, question 4, in Opera omnia, vol. 4 (Vatican City, 1956), pp. 230-277
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit identifies this question, on distinguishing the divine Persons, as the passage behind the thesis, citing Farmer's own note to the same effect.

doctrine: The thesis holds that it is compatible with Catholic truth to say the divine Persons are distinguished by 'absolute properties' rather than by relations alone (edelheit2022:13850). Farmer's note observes that the phrase in divinis is best rendered simply 'in God,' and places the thesis in a series on Trinitarian distinction beginning at 2.1 (farmer1998:12214).
context: Edelheit calls the thesis 'crucial for understanding one of Pico's main lines of argumentation in the Apology,' since it establishes that a view unsupported by an explicit authority is not thereby shown false: 'it is clear that this issue is not regarded negatively by authority' (edelheit2022:13910).
historiography: Edelheit locates the source discussion in Scotus's Ordinatio 1, distinction 8, part 1, question 4, on the tension between divine simplicity and the distinction of Persons (edelheit2022:13850, 13874), a passage he says Farmer had already indicated (edelheit2022:13874).

quotations.text: In thesis 3 we find that arguing that the three Persons in the Trinity are distinguished in divine absolute properties is not against the Catholic truth.
